slots.title: Background
b1Text: The city opened its bike share in 2019 with forty stations and four hundred bikes. Riders took more trips every year, and the busiest month was always June. Students and commuters make up most members, while visitors buy day passes. Each station has room for twelve bikes and a screen that shows the nearest dock.

The council pays for the docks, and a private firm runs the fleet on contract. Repairs take two days on average, and a van moves bikes from full stations at night. Electric bikes were added in 2022 and now make up a third of all trips. A yearly pass costs sixty euros, and a single ride costs one euro.

Electric bikes were added in 2022 and now make up a third of all trips. A yearly pass costs sixty euros, and a single ride costs one euro. Surveys show that nine in ten riders would recommend the service to a friend. The main complaint is that docks near the station are often full in the morning. Crime is low: fewer than twenty bikes a year are stolen or lost.
